reason: Verified in source and frames. lately.html line 721 renders `Full briefing` next to `Today’s Signal` on line 720; the light-full frames at 1440 and 390 show 'Today's Signal Full briefing Lately' exactly as claimed. This is not taste: the repo's own URL and naming contract (docs/SUITE_URL_AND_NAMING_CONTRACT.md, lines 18 and 57-58) states the briefing surfaces are named 'Today's Signal' (inside Home) and 'Full Briefing' (/app/home/briefing), and this brief's own non-negotiable architecture clause writes 'a tab strip beside Today's Signal and the Full Briefing'. The artifact also capitalises every other product name it prints (Tasks, Timeline, Notes in the coverage row), so sentence case here is not a house rule the tab is following - it is the one label out of step. The string lives in the shared shell() template, so it is wrong in all seven states and both grounds, on the page's second line. Neither gate touches it: audit.mjs has no copy assertion and interaction-check.mjs never reads the tab text, so this is exactly the class of defect automation cannot see. Severity is corrected upward from the seat's 'refinement' to 'defect': by the panel's own definitions refinement means nothing is wrong, and here the product misnames one of its own surfaces against a written contract - visibly wrong, but the reader still reaches the right place, so it stops short of misleading. The proposed fix is the right one and needs no sharpening: one character, matching the contract and the sibling tab.
breaks: Nothing structural. The change is one glyph ('b' to 'B') in the shell() template, adding roughly 1px to the tab's advance width; the 390x844 frame shows the strip ending well short of the fold, so there is no wrap or overflow risk at the narrow end, and 768/1280/1440 have more room still. Re-measure after it lands: run audit.mjs (type ramp, leading and hit-target checks touch the tab strip's box) and re-shoot the seven light states plus the dark ground, since the string is shared by all of them - a diff on any one state that does not move by the same sub-pixel amount would mean the label is duplicated somewhere the grep missed. Worth chasing in the same cycle for consistency, though outside the graded artifact: plan.html line 387 prints 'Full briefing' in its own prose.
